symptom: `refresh catalog full source force` on an unchanged project described a project pluggable widget as `pluggablewidget '<id>' name` on some runs and by its keyword on others; once cached, the incremental build kept the wrong row.
cause: captureDescribeParallel built a fresh ExecContext per describe, so each of up to eight workers loaded its own widget registry; one unstamped .def.json (hand-made, or its .mpk gone) made every load call RefreshWidgetDefinitions(force), which truncated and rewrote every definition (os.WriteFile) while the other workers read them. A torn read aborted LoadUserDefinitions, its error discarded, so that describe's registry lacked the widget and pluggableWidgetHeader fell back as designed.
insight: The tell was the SHAPE: two of twenty widgets, all on one page — a per-describe input going bad, not a broken lookup (that hits all twenty). It did not reproduce on a clean project; it needs a definition that stays stale forever. `strace -e trace=openat` settled it in one run: 16 writes and 30 reads of one .def.json during a single build. A per-goroutine clone of a context silently re-runs every lazy loader it holds — copy the loaded state in, and load it before the fan-out.
